name: Red dunes
summary: Orange dunes just outside town: walk the slope and sandboard at sunset for the late-day color. Đồi cát bay sits in Mui Ne ward, a field of about 36.8 ha. The 2019 ministry workshop places it about 22 km from the Phan Thiet city center. Vietnam Tourism calls the same dunes just outside town. Give the slope the end of the day. Bàu Trắng is the dawn ride.
getThere: A ride from the strip. About 22 km from the Phan Thiet center.
heroCaption: Orange slope, casuarinas, and walkers on the sand

notice.title: Come for the sunset
notice.body: Vietnam Tourism sends you here as the sun drops past the horizon. Bàu Trắng is the 5:00–7:00 ride.

body: Walk the orange slope and sandboard as the sun drops. Vietnam Tourism sends you to the red dunes just outside town for that late light. The 2019 ministry workshop names the field Đồi cát bay, about 36.8 ha in Mui Ne ward, and says that since 2016 it has been assigned to the provincial youth outdoor center, overlapping the Ham Tien–Mui Ne tourism board and the ward.

The 22 km figure on that workshop page is measured from the Phan Thiet city center. The ride from a resort gate on the Ham Tien strip is its own trip. Bàu Trắng, in Hoa Thang, is the dawn field. This slope is the sunset.

gettingThere: Đồi cát bay is the orange field in Mui Ne ward. Vietnam Tourism calls the red dunes just outside town. The 2019 ministry workshop places the field about 22 km from the Phan Thiet city center.
Vietnam Tourism names a motorbike for the dunes and the coast. The 22 km line is from the city center, so the ride from the Ham Tien strip is separate.
